body:
Follow-up to #6271, as proposed in https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/pull/6271#issuecomment-6284710739.

## What this adds

`OceananigansMakieExt` can now plot a horizontal field on a `YinYangGrid`, or on an `ImmersedBoundaryGrid` wrapping one:

```julia
fig = Figure()
ax = Axis3(fig[1, 1]; aspect=:data)
quadmesh!(ax, view(T, :, :, Nz); colormap=:thermal, nan_color=:gray)
```

- `quadmesh!(ax, f::YinYangField)` draws both panels as one flat-shaded mesh on the sphere. Yin draws the cells it owns. Yang, just beneath it, draws the cells in which it owns any area (from `owned_weights`), so the overlap is drawn once. Both panels go into one mesh because CairoMakie orders triangles by depth within a plot but not across plots.
- Each cell is a quad of one color between its panel's corners. The plot shows the data as the panels hold it, with no interpolation between cell centers.
- Immersed cells are masked with `NaN` panel by panel, following the existing `mask_immersed_field!` pattern.
- `quadmesh!(ax, f::Observable{<:YinYangField})` builds the mesh once and updates only the colors, for animations.
- `geo_surface!` and `surface!(::Axis3, ...)` dispatch to the same method for Yin-Yang fields, so `geo_surface(f)` works too.
- Fields must be at `(Center, Center)` horizontally and have a single vertical index. Anything else throws an `ArgumentError`.

## Example

`examples/yin_yang_grid.jl` drops its hand-built `sphere_point`, `cell_quads` and `panel_mesh`, along with the `land=` mask. It now stores 2D snapshot fields (`Field{Center, Center, Nothing}`, filled with `set!` from a surface `view`) and plots them with `quadmesh!`. The Double Drake continents are masked automatically because the snapshots live on the immersed grid.

## Tests

A new testset in `test/makie/makie.jl` checks:
- quad counts against `owned_weights`
- Yin vertices on the sphere and Yang vertices just beneath it
- that only the immersed polar cap is masked
- that the drawn quads cover the sphere's area (between 0.99 × 4π and 1.2 × 4π)
- `Observable` color updates
- the `geo_surface!`, `geo_surface` and `surface!` entry points
- the `ArgumentError`s

All 127 tests in the file pass locally on CPU.

body:
## What this fixes

A regular coordinate was a range starting at the first halo face, so its nodes depended in the last bit on the halo
size, and each rank of a distributed grid built its own range from a rounded local interval. So:

- a grid copied with a wider halo (`with_halo`, which the split-explicit free surface uses in connected directions)
  had nodes and metrics a few ulps from those of the grid it came from;
- the ranks of a distributed grid had nodes and metrics a few ulps from those of the same grid on one rank.

Fields set from node positions (an interpolated initial condition, for one) then differed from the serial ones at
~1e-13 from the first step.

## Changes

- The faces of a regular coordinate are `range(c₁, c₂, length = N + 1)`, extended into the halos with the same
  reference and step; the centers lie half a step from them. The interior nodes, ends included, no longer depend on
  the halo, and the end faces are exactly `c₁` and `c₂`.
- `partition_coordinate` returns, for an interval, a `PartitionedInterval`, and each rank evaluates the nodes of the
  whole coordinate at its own indices.

## Tests

- `test/unit/grids.jl`: `with_halo` keeps the nodes of a `LatitudeLongitudeGrid`, and its end faces are the given
  bounds.
- `test/mpi/architectures.jl`: each rank's nodes, areas and spacings equal those of the grid on one rank.

Both fail on `main`.

body:
Metal has no Float64, so moving a Float64 host array to a Metal architecture failed. For example, setting a Float32 Metal field from a Float64 array:

```julia
grid = RectilinearGrid(GPU(Metal.MetalBackend()), size=(4, 4, 4), extent=(1, 1, 1))
set!(CenterField(grid), rand(4, 4, 4))
# ERROR: Metal does not support Float64 values, try using Float32 instead
```

This came up setting a bathymetry computed in Float64 on the CPU onto a Float32 Metal grid. `on_architecture(::MetalGPU, ::Array{Float64})` now converts to Float32, as the extension already does for `StepRangeLen`. This fixes every caller that moves host arrays to Metal, not only `set!`.

Adds a test to `test/metal/metal.jl`. Locally on an M5 Max it fails on v0.114.1 with the error above and passes with this change.

title: Convert Float64 arrays to Float32 when moving them to Metal
